contract: No view is canonical. Each names the module that produced it and what that module assumes.
Cross-view relations are explicit rather than merged.
Disagreements between views are listed and left standing. They are the evidence that the views are independent readings.

geometry.assumes: wall ownership and sector loops as the MAP records them

assemblies.assumes: an assembly is what a sector contains, references by marker, and is wired to by channel

functional_regions.assumes: structure is recovered from floor heights and portal adjacency; nothing about triggers or channels
limitations: detection is static: transient door and lift motion is ignored
a stepped run is a measured climb, not a claim that the designer drew a staircase
a recess is a small dead end; whether it reads as an alcove is not measured here
residual records how far the original is from its own parameters, not whether that matters

facades.assumes: a facade is a maximal collinear run of one sky-lit sector's wall loop, at least two 1024 bays long

effects.assumes: the name comes from the embedding, never the fields; rotate and slide are returned undecided

conditional_topology.assumes: portal_graph, minus crossings whose wall carries the blocking cstat, plus those blocking walls a kWallGib mechanism reopens. The default.

summary.base_assumes: portal_graph, minus crossings whose wall carries the blocking cstat, plus those blocking walls a kWallGib mechanism reopens. The default.

progression.assumes: rounds are ordered; the actions inside a round are not, so this is not a play order

sp_understand.assumes: spatial.walkable_at_rest plus channel-opened extras; known_non_portal_transitions are not read

visual.assumes: a viewpoint is placed only where a body has standing clearance at rest; a frame is what the editor renderer painted with the local game data, not design intent

refused.reason: no interior point with standing clearance

disagreements.about: how much of the map a body can end up reaching
disagreements.why_they_can_differ: different base graphs. The conditional view gates on the wall blocking cstat and reopens what a mechanism drives; analyze_progression floods spatial.walkable_at_rest, which also refuses portals under 512 wide or 4096 of opening, and never reads known_non_portal_transitions, so stack links and teleports are invisible to it.

both refuse the rotate and slide families for the same reason -- their spatial questions are about a vertical opening -- but they count different things: effects counts mechanisms it declines to name, the conditional view counts mechanisms whose crossings it leaves in the base ungated. Neither number is a claim that those mechanisms do nothing.

disagreements.about: sectors both a street frontage and a structural shape
disagreements.why_they_can_differ: a facade is read from a sky-lit sector's wall loop and a structure from floor heights and adjacency. One sector being both is the two views cutting the same space differently, which is the point of keeping both.

disagreements.about: sectors the geometry calls player space that the traversal never reaches
disagreements.why_they_can_differ: sector_kinds asks whether a sector looks like player space; the conditional frontier asks whether a body can get there through gates it can open. A sector reachable only by riding a rotor, or over a blocked wall no mechanism drives, is player space this traversal cannot enter.

disagreements.about: places the renderer will not stand where another view makes a claim

refused.reason: no interior point with standing clearance

disagreements.why_they_can_differ: the observer places a viewpoint only where a body has standing clearance at rest. A sector the conditional view calls a way through, shut until something opens it, has nowhere to stand until then -- so a refusal here agrees with the gate rather than contradicting it.
